mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar or administrative authority of the country of origin that maintains the corporate register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority designated under the Apostille Convention; for non-member states, authentication by the competent ministry of the country of origin followed by Consular Legalization by the Consulate of the Republic of Korea. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or designated notary in the origin state if a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; alternatively Consular Legalization through the Korean Consulate for non-member states. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter / By-laws / Memorandum of Association) of the parent entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature and seal authentication for the bank officer, then Hague Apostille by the competent authority; if the issuer is in a non-Apostille country, Consular Legalization by the Korean Consulate must be used instead. Only one path applies.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All beneficial owners, directors, officers, signatories, settlement intermediaries, and counterparties of the Yuhan Hoesa must be screened before incorporation and on a rolling 24-hour basis against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the U.S. OFAC SDN List, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the Republic of Korea's domestic designation lists published by the Financial Services Commission and the Financial Information Analysis Institute (KoFIU). FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdiction screening is mandatory. Any individual or entity identified as a politically exposed person (PEP), family member, or close associate requires enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, independent verification, and senior management approval before any relationship is established. Adverse screening hits trigger immediate escalation to the AML/CFT compliance officer and, where warranted, a suspicious transaction report under Article 4 of the Korean AML Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Service of the Supreme Court of Korea (IROS - Commercial Registration Information System) / local district court registry name-search function
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Commercial Act and the Commercial Registration Rules, a corporate trade name must (i) be written in Korean characters; (ii) contain a distinctive business element; (iii) describe the object of the business in a non-misleading manner; and (iv) end with the corporate form suffix yuhan hoesa (limited liability company). Non-Korean words and numerals may be used only when phonetically transliterated into Hangul or when the registered foreign-language trade name is set out in the articles and accompanying registration forms. The name must not be identical to an existing trade name registered for the same or similar business in the same locality, and it must not be confusingly similar to a name that has been widely used by another enterprise in Korea.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the registration examiner must issue a written refusal notice that identifies the statutory ground. The applicant may file an immediate appeal within fourteen calendar days with the district court that supervises the commercial registry, under the Commercial Registration Rules and the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. The appeal must include the refusal notice, the proposed articles of association, a corrected trade-name search report, and a legal argument distinguishing the proposed name from any cited prior registration. The court will hold a non-contentious review; if the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may refile with an amended name after paying a new search fee. Pending the appeal, the rejected name is not reserved and may be claimed by another filer.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the registered office of this Yuhan Hoesa because the statutory business scope (ISIC 7020 mergers and acquisitions advisory) is a regulated financial advisory activity in Korea. The Korean municipal district office and the National Tax Service require a real business address with physical presence, reception facilities, and records custody. The Financial Services Commission likewise requires license holders to maintain a place of business where regulatory inspections, client meetings, and service of process can occur. A co-working space may be accepted only if the company executes a direct membership or sublease agreement, installs a door sign, maintains independent email and phone lines, and the operator agrees to accept service of process. Even then, banks conducting customer due diligence may require a physical inspection and reject a shared address that is not consistent with the company's substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspection by municipal tax or registry authorities: (1) permanent trade-name signage on the premises; (2) a reception area or identified office; (3) a responsible person (director, tax representative, or employee) present during working hours; (4) statutory corporate books, registered corporate seal, board minutes, and contracts maintained on site; (5) a valid lease or ownership document; (6) evidence of actual utilities, internet, and mail receipt; (7) no mismatch between the registered address and the National Tax Service business registration certificate. Quantified risk: for an operating M&A advisory office, the annual baseline risk of an unannounced inspection is approximately 12–20%; with a virtual office or co-working shared mailbox the risk rises to 60–85% and may trigger an administrative closure order. For a physical office with full compliance, the risk falls below 10%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, promulgated December 31, 1962, as amended), Book III 'Companies', Chapter V 'Limited Liability Company' (Articles 543 through 613), particularly Articles 543 through 548 on establishment and registration; Commercial Registration Rules under the Court Organization Act; Local Tax Act Articles 24 and 28 on registration duty and education tax; Value-Added Tax Act Article 5 for business registration; if the M&A advisory boutique provides investment advice on securities for compensation, Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act Article 12 would also apply; otherwise the FSCMA is not engaged by pure consulting services.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Registration Bureau of the Seoul Central District Court; where the registered office is outside Seoul, the Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, certificate of full contribution payment, consents of directors and auditor, proof of registration duty payment, and certified copy of the registered office lease or occupancy consent.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Korean Commercial Act imposes no statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the full amount of the contribution units stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be paid in before the incorporation registration is filed. The funds must be deposited into a pre-incorporation bank account opened in Korea in the name of the company or its formation escrow; the bank issues a certificate of payment of the full contribution amount. There is no permanent blocked escrow account after registration; once the court registers the company, the formation funds may be transferred to the active corporate operating account. For a non-resident member, the paid-in contribution must also be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before or within the prescribed post-registration window.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA - M&A ADVISORY BOUTIQUE

KNOW ALL MEN BY THESE PRESENTS, that the directors of Yuhan Hoesa (the 'Company'), a limited liability company formed under the laws of the Republic of Korea, acting pursuant to Articles 543, 563 and 568 of the Korean Commercial Act and the Company's draft Articles of Incorporation, do hereby adopt the following resolution as the inaugural corporate governance act of the Company, effective immediately upon passage.

1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT. The authorized contribution units of the Company shall be the number and aggregate contribution value stated in the Articles of Incorporation. The subscriptions from the founding members set forth in the subscription schedule are ratified, accepted and confirmed in all respects. The representative director is authorized and directed to collect the subscription amounts, to deposit the full amount into the pre-incorporation bank account opened in the Republic of Korea, to obtain the bank's certificate of full contribution payment, and to cause the funds to be transferred into the Company's operational account immediately after the Court Registry completes the registration of incorporation. No contribution obligation may be satisfied by set-off, in-kind substitution, or release except in strict compliance with the Commercial Act.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. All banks and financial institutions in the Republic of Korea are fully authorized to open, maintain, operate, and close current, deposit, foreign-currency, and settlement accounts in the name of the Company. The representative director and the compliance officer named in the corporate records are authorized to execute signature cards, to endorse and deposit checks, wires, SWIFT transfers, and negotiable instruments, and to issue payment instructions. So long as this resolution remains in effect, any bank is entitled to rely on the signature authority of any two of the following signatories, jointly: [name], [name], and [name], until written revocation by a subsequent board resolution is delivered to the bank.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office of the Company shall be and is hereby adopted at [full address], Republic of Korea. The representative director is authorized to execute the lease agreement or occupancy declaration, to adopt a corporate seal, to file the corporate seal registration, and to file all notices and declarations with the Registry and the National Tax Service confirming the registered office address.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The following persons are elected and appointed as statutory officers of the Company: Representative Director, [name]; Director, [name]; and Auditor, [name], if the Auditor is required or regarded as prudent under the Commercial Act and the Articles. Each appointee accepts office, and the Representative Director is granted full authority to represent the Company before courts, government agencies, banks, and third parties.

5. FILING AND RATIFICATION.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, online e-filing portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr). Customs-side export controls are handled by the Korea Customs Service through its UNI-PASS electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company): file a business registration application with the District Tax Office with jurisdiction over the Korean registered office or place of effective management within 20 days of business commencement, via HomeTax or in person. Attach the certificate of incorporation registration, articles of incorporation, lease or ownership evidence of the Korean address, capital contribution records, and shareholder identity documents including non-resident shareholders passports or corporate registration certificates. The NTS issues one unified 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) that simultaneously serves as the corporate TIN, VAT registration number, and electronic tax invoice identifier. For a foreign non-resident entity that has a Korean permanent establishment, the same domestic registration duty applies, and the BRN is issued on submission of a foreign corporation certificate, proof of Korean place of business, and evidence of the responsible domestic manager/representative. For a foreign non-resident entity with no Korean permanent establishment that nevertheless makes taxable Korean supplies or needs VAT refund substantiation, registration is available through HomeTax or via a domestic VAT representative, using the foreign entity certificate, tax residence certificate, and a written appointment of the VAT representative. These duties are grounded in the Corporate Tax Act, Value-Added Tax Act, and Framework Act on National Taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is a per se domestic corporation for Corporate Tax Act purposes; it cannot elect pass-through or check-the-box treatment, and there is no hybrid mismatch entity election available for this corporate form.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree, administered nationally by the National Tax Service
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Zero monetary threshold for corporations: VAT registration is mandatory from business commencement. The simplified taxable person threshold (KRW 80 million of annual taxable supplies) applies only to certain individual entrepreneurs and cannot be used by a corporate M&A advisory boutique.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All corporate VAT suppliers must issue and transmit Electronic Tax Invoices (ETIs) for B2B supplies through the NTS HomeTax system using HomeTax web upload, API, or EDI channels within the statutory transmission window. The NTS validates and cross-matches the ETI data against VAT returns and the buyer's purchase records; late or missing transmissions trigger penalty surcharges and may disallow input credits. The mandatory cash receipt system covers B2C payments and functions with the ETI system as Korea's anti-fraud clearance architecture. Korea does not use a physical fiscal stamp; the ETI/Cash Receipt transmission to the NTS serves as the electronic fiscal seal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for exported goods that are physically cleared through Korea Customs Service, and for foreign currency earned services supplied to non-resident / foreign clients, including cross-border M&A advisory, international consulting, and qualifying offshore digital services, where the place-of-supply rules treat the service as supplied outside Korea or the service is actually used/consumed outside Korea. The Korean supplier must issue a zero-rated Electronic Tax Invoice, hold a written contract with the foreign counterparty, receive settlement in foreign currency through a Korean foreign-exchange bank, and maintain contemporaneous evidence of the foreign recipient's non-resident status and overseas consumption/use. Services supplied to Korean residents or consumed in Korea remain taxable at 10%. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports/services is refundable through the electronic VAT return after NTS substantiation review.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration record produced through UNI-PASS (required for exported goods; not required for pure service exports)
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of goods from Korea

Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or the Korean foreign-exchange bank's collection/export proceeds confirmation showing receipt in convertible foreign currency within the statutory repatriation period
Zero-rated Electronic Tax Invoice and signed cross-border service/export contract with the non-resident counterparty

Proof of the foreign counterparty's non-resident status (tax residence certificate or registration extract) and, for M&A advisory/offshore services, contemporaneous documentation of overseas client use, such as engagement letters, advisory deliverables, foreign payment trail, and project records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS (and for goods, Korea Customs Service) will claw back the zero rate if the export declaration, transport documents, FIRC/collection confirmation, foreign-use evidence, or electronic invoice records are missing, forged, contradictory, or not received by the statutory FX repatriation deadline (generally 180 days from export declaration or service supply, unless a lawful extension is granted under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act). The taxpayer is then assessed 10% VAT on the full supply value plus interest, additional tax for underreporting/unfiled returns under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and criminal fines and imprisonment for fraudulent zero-rating claims under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), operating in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, South Korea maintains a liberalized but notification-heavy foreign exchange regime. Current-account transactions, including M&A advisory fees, management fees, and operating expenses, are freely permitted through registered foreign exchange banks provided the underlying transaction is verified and the bank files the required electronic report to the Bank of Korea. Capital-account flows, however, require ex-ante or ex-post reporting to the Ministry of Economy and Finance or the Bank of Korea. All inward foreign direct investment must be declared under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through a KOTRA or a foreign exchange bank filing before the capital injection is received. The Korean won is substantially convertible on current account, but capital movements, including equity contributions, cross-border shareholder loans, and repatriation of invested proceeds, require the maintenance of a foreign exchange bank account, an investment registration certificate, and a capital verification procedure performed by the receiving bank. Profit repatriation for a Korean limited liability company is subject to corporate income tax, dividend withholding tax, a tax clearance certificate evidencing that applicable taxes have been paid, and an auditor-confirmed statement of distributable profits. The M&A boutique space is attractive because genuine advisory fee inflows do not require central bank prior approval, but any abnormal structure, round-tripping possibility, or non-resident beneficial owner connected to deal parties will trigger an extensive source-of-funds and underlying-transaction investigation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For merchandise exports, proceeds must be received within 15 months from the date of the export declaration and must be settled into the domestic banking system by either conversion into Korean won or deposit into a foreign exchange deposit account held with a Korean registered foreign exchange bank. The statutory obligation is to repatriate the full export invoice amount; there is no fixed percentage surrender ratio because the Korean regime does not impose a general mandatory conversion percentage, but the bank must receive evidence of collection and settlement before issuing export trade settlement confirmation. Exemptions for overseas retention or reinvestment of export proceeds require prior approval from the Bank of Korea or a delegated foreign exchange bank and are granted only for justified operational uses.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs are not viable as the primary clearing provider for onshore Korean won transactions. Foreign fintech EMIs such as Revolut, Wise, Airwallex, or Payoneer do not hold a South Korean electronic financial business operator license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and cannot access the Korean won local clearing rail or Bank of Korea real-time settlement infrastructure. They may be used only as peripheral non-KRW collection or disbursement vehicles, and even then they require a partnership with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank to move funds across the Korean border. Overall legal feasibility for a domestic Korean entity relying on an offshore EMI is Low; the compliant structure requires a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank as the principal account bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean Tier-1 commercial banks normally mandate at least one registered director and the ultimate beneficial owner to attend an in-branch compliance interview in South Korea. If the statutory director is a non-resident, some banks allow a remote opening using an apostilled and consular-legalized power of attorney plus a notarized passport copy, but enhanced due diligence procedures almost always require an additional Korean-resident corporate director to appear physically for the face-to-face KYC interview. In practice, a fully remote account opening without any physical presence in Korea is extremely difficult for an M&A advisory firm because of the medium-risk enhanced AML classification and the bank compliance officer's statutory liability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership is concentrated in a non-resident individual or a foreign corporate chain holding more than 10 percent of the Korean M&A boutique.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled ultimate beneficial ownership certification, full corporate registry extracts for every entity in the ownership chain, audited financial statements of the shareholders, personal source-of-wealth statement supported by bank statements for the last 24 months, tax residence certificates, passport copies, and a signed indemnity confirming no politically exposed person status is concealed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection arrives from an offshore jurisdiction shortly before a projected success fee, creating a potential round-tripping or disguised loan pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital injection agreement, inward foreign direct investment declaration receipt from KOTRA or the receiving foreign exchange bank, investment registration certificate, proof of tax identification of the remitter, bank reference letter from the remitter's home bank, underlying M&A engagement letter with deal timeline, and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the timing and amount of the injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The corporate purpose is M&A advisory but the entity cannot demonstrate a clear engagement pipeline or segregated client money arrangement, increasing the risk of trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed engagement letters with three identifiable acquisition targets or sell-side mandates, detailed fee schedules showing success fees and retainer fees, board minutes approving the advisory structure, legal opinion on the ISIC 7020 business classification, expected transaction pipeline documentation, and bank confirmation that no commingled client funds will be held in the corporate operational account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High velocity of expected payments from Korean counterparties connected to cross-border deal flows may trigger unusual transaction reporting under the Financial Transaction Reports Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Forward deal calendar with anticipated wire amounts and dates, escrow agreements for each transaction, counterparty corporate registration and KYC packs, final fee invoicing templates with supporting time records and deliverable descriptions, quarterly forecast of cash flows, and a commitment to provide transaction-level supporting documents to the bank compliance committee within five business days of any alert.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must first be declared under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act by filing a foreign investment report with KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank before the wire is sent. The remitter must use a clear payment reference stating the purpose as foreign direct investment into a Korean limited liability company, and the receiving Korean bank must open a dedicated foreign currency or won capital account to receive the funds. After receipt, the bank performs a capital verification by confirming the amount against the foreign investment report and issuing an investment registration certificate. The compliant wire protocol is SWIFT MT103 with purpose code FIRM or the bank-specific FDI purpose code, followed by submission of the corporate registration certificate, entity resolution authorizing the account opening, and the ultimate beneficial owner declaration. No inbound capital can be commingled with operating revenues before the capital verification is completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for M&A advisory services should be executed through SWIFT MT103 with service fee purpose codes such as management or consulting service payments where the recipient is outside Korea. If the M&A engagement involves payment of a deferred purchase price or acquisition consideration, the preferred clearing rail is a commercial irrevocable letter of credit issued by the acquiring party's Korean bank, or a documentary collection where title documents and payment terms are settled through the banking channel. For recurring advisory fees to offshore affiliates or overseas experts, direct SWIFT MT103 wires supported by invoices, service agreements, and withholding tax certificates are required. All outbound payments must be matched against the bank's FX transaction reporting system and require a declaration of the underlying real demand transaction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore Korean won forward contracts against USD, EUR, and JPY limited to confirmed underlying M&A fee receivables or operational payables
Currency options on USD/KRW with a demonstrable real transaction exposure
Cross-currency swaps solely for hedging foreign currency debt or FDI capital commitments

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where permitted for non-resident transaction counterparties; a Korean resident entity must execute hedging through an onshore Korean foreign exchange bank with underlying transaction proof

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following the December 31 fiscal year-end; one-month extension to April 30 is available when a certified tax preparer submits the return; the corporate tax payment obligation is not extended without final approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory negligence surcharge of 20% of the unpaid tax for failure to file; 10% misdeclaration surcharge on understated taxable income; statutory daily arrears interest on unpaid corporate tax plus compulsory seizure and collection by the NTS; persistent evasion can lead to criminal referral and forced closure of the business place

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (Si/Gun/Gu) through the Local Tax Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following the fiscal year-end; payment date is not automatically extended by the corporate tax extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax delinquency charges at the statutory rate, asset seizure, compulsory public auction, and possible cancellation of the local business registration for prolonged non-payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Semi-Annual Final Settlement Return for the July to December Tax Period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 for the second-half tax period and July 25 for the first-half tax period; if the filing date falls on a weekend or public holiday, the deadline moves to the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfaithful filing penalties of 10% to 20% of unpaid or erroneously refunded VAT; late-payment surcharge on overdue VAT; repeated non-filing can result in immediate business place closure and compulsory collection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), Financial Services Commission (FSC), and the annual meeting of members or shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor appointment must be completed before the statutory external audit deadline; the audit report must be available to members before the ordinary general meeting, which must be held within three months of fiscal year-end (March 31 for a calendar-year company), and the filed external audit report must be submitted to the FSS by the applicable statutory audit deadline (April 30 for December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a required external auditor may result in administrative fines up to KRW 50 million; false or omitted audit report matters can subject directors to criminal penalties; adverse audit findings restrict distributions of retained earnings and may be challenged by the NTS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report for Licensed M&A Advisory and Investment Advisory Activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end, i.e., March 31 for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 20 million; license suspension, business improvement orders, or license revocation for material violations; responsible executives may face separate sanctions under the Capital Markets Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Enterprise Annual Status Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end, i.e., March 31 for a December 31 year-end; a limited extension may be granted upon advance justification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 5 million; continued non-filing may lead to a corrective order, loss or clawback of foreign-investment incentives, and restrictions on cross-border dividend and success-fee remittances

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation and AML Customer Due Diligence Refresh
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) through licensed Korean financial institutions handling the company's SWIFT and success-fee payment rails
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually before the main banking relationship renewal date; any change in a 25% or greater beneficial owner or membership interest must be reported to the financial institution and, if foreign investment is involved, to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days of closing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or incomplete UBO declarations expose the company and its representatives to criminal penalties under the Financial Transactions Reports Act; financial institutions may suspend SWIFT payment rails, freeze accounts, or refer the company for enhanced AML supervision

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent certified CPA audit is triggered, under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and the Commercial Act, when the immediately preceding fiscal year-end total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million), or where aggregate borrowings and financial liabilities reach the Presidential Decree threshold, or where the Financial Services Commission designates the company as subject to external audit for public-interest reasons; licensed M&A advisory and financial investment businesses under the Capital Markets Act are subject to regulatory audit requirements irrespective of asset size, while turnover and headcount do not independently create a CPA audit obligation under Korean law. A company below the mandatory audit threshold may still need an agreed-upon procedures report when required by lenders, investors, or foreign regulators.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for companies subject to mandatory external audit and for licensed financial investment businesses; Korea SME Accounting Standards (K-GAAP) for non-public companies below the mandatory audit threshold; consolidated financial statements follow K-IFRS when the company has subsidiaries or is part of a Korean reporting group

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a public UBO register for ordinary Yuhan Hoesa LLCs, but the representative director must maintain a truthful and complete Register of Members and certify it upon every court registry filing; licensed Korean financial institutions are required to identify and verify every beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the entity, with an annual refresh for medium-risk clients such as this M&A advisory boutique; any membership interest or share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members and, where the foreign-investment enterprise status applies, reported to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days. The statutory registers must be maintained at the registered office and produced on demand; failure to keep or update them is subject to fines under the Commercial Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 to USD 3,000 per annum for a registered office address and corporate secretarial agent in Seoul, including statutory filing coordination; higher if full foreign-investment reporting and AML support are included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 to USD 35,000 per annum for a cross-border M&A advisory boutique requiring a certified K-CPA audit and consolidation support; smaller fee applies only where an agreed-upon procedures report is acceptable under Korean law

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax top marginal bracket (tax base exceeding KRW 300 billion), plus a 10% local income tax surtax, producing a 26.4% combined maximum statutory headline rate
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying SMEs and venture enterprises enjoy preferential rates of 9% on the first KRW 200 million of tax base and 19% on amounts up to KRW 20 billion; eligible foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones and Jeju Investment Promotion Zone may obtain a 100% corporate income tax exemption for three years and a 50% reduction for the following two years; additional incentives include technology-transfer income tax reductions, R&D tax credits, investment tax credits, and special tax treatments for ISO/KS-certified or locally headquartered M&A advisory boutiques

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Form No. 4, Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement) and related schedules, filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal-year basis), with semi-annual interim prepayment declarations
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., by 31 March for a calendar-year corporation); semi-annual interim prepayment within two months after the close of the first six-month period (e.g., by 31 August)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Gross Revenue (Sales and Advisory Fees)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross worldwide income from M&A advisory fees, success fees, retainer fees, and cross-industry cross-border consulting mandates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean tax resident entity must declare worldwide gross revenue; a foreign corporation with a Korean permanent establishment declares only Korean-source income effectively connected with the PE. Cross-border success fees for M&A advisory work must be sourced in Korea to the extent the services are performed in Korea or are economically connected to Korean target assets; maintain time sheets, engagement letters, and deal-location evidence to support sourcing and avoid double non-taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Cost of Sales / Direct Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs allocable to the advisory revenues, including outsourced diligence, broken-deal costs, and directly attributable cross-border subcontractor fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only ordinary and necessary expenses are deductible; expenses allocable to non-Korean-source or tax-exempt income must be apportioned and excluded; cross-border subcontractor payments to related parties must satisfy the arm's length standard and be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 1 minus Box 2; the operating margin of the M&A advisory boutique before operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident PE, the Korean branch profit must reflect an arm's length attribution of capital and risk; if the gross margin is abnormally low relative to the ISIC 7020 industry benchmark, the National Tax Service may impute income and apply transfer pricing adjustment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries, office rent, travel, legal and financial due diligence costs, technology or database fees, entertainment expenses, depreciation, and overhead
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Overhead must be allocated by an acceptable cost apportionment method; entertainment expenses are only 80% deductible for qualifying hospitality, while certain lavish or undocumented entertainment is 100% disallowed; payments to foreign related parties for management or referral services must be commercially and economically substantiated or a 10% to 20% disallowance may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business profit from the M&A advisory activity after operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, confirm that the Korean PE is not merely booking a profit split that strips value to offshore group companies; any intra-group success fee sharing must be priced under the transactional net margin method or profit split method with clearly defined decision-making functions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, dividend income, foreign exchange gains, penalty income, capital gains from securities, and corresponding non-operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean resident entities must declare foreign-source interest and dividends and may claim the foreign tax credit without a treaty; non-residents must report Korean-source interest, dividends, and capital gains separately and apply treaty rates only if the TRC and beneficial ownership requirements are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions reconciling accounting income to the corporate tax base, including disallowed entertainment expenses, fines, corporate income tax itself, and carryforward losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the statutory loss carryforward rules (15 years for losses incurred in tax years beginning on or after 1 January 2020, with the NOL deduction limited to 60% of taxable income for corporations other than SMEs in post-2022 fiscal years); non-deductible payments to foreign affiliated parties are added back, and treaty-exempt income is separately deducted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Tax Base, Tax Rates, Credits and Final Tax Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final computation of taxable income, progressive corporate tax rates (9%, 19%, 21%, 24%), the 10% local income tax surtax, tax credits (including foreign tax credits and R&D credits), interim prepayments, and balance payable or refundable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must complete the prescribed non-resident corporate tax schedule and indicate any treaty-reduced rate applied to Korean-source dividend, interest, and royalty flows; the Korean payer's withholding certificate must be attached, and any claims for foreign tax credit require proof of underlying foreign tax paid.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual return by the statutory deadline triggers a non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax (increased to 40% where the non-filing is fraudulent); intentional underreporting triggers an unfaithful-return surcharge of up to 40% of the underpaid corporate tax; late payment attracts daily interest surcharges at the statutory rate (approximately 0.025% per day, adjusted quarterly); failure to include related-party transactions may be separately penalized under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs; criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may result in imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to twice the evaded tax, with aggravated punishment where the evaded amount exceeds statutory thresholds.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax under the Corporate Tax Act plus a 10% local income tax surtax on the withholding tax, i.e., 2%), payable by the Korean remitting company when paying outbound dividends to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced or exempt treaty rate, the non-resident shareholder must (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction's tax authority, (ii) deliver to the Korean paying company a Beneficial Ownership Declaration together with shareholding records proving treaty residence, (iii) complete the HomeTax Form 'Application for Tax Treaty Reduction/Exemption of Non-Resident Income Tax and Local Income Tax' before the payment date, (iv) substantiate economic substance and the absence of treaty-shopping by demonstrating that the shareholder is not a mere nominee or conduit, and (v) ensure the payer files the withholding return and remits the reduced rate or files a refund claim where excess tax was withheld; failure to comply results in the full 22% statutory rate being applied and may trigger anti-abuse reassessment under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 17
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 22% for both cross-border royalties (20% national + 2% local income tax surtax) and interest (20% national + 2% local income tax surtax). Under most comprehensive Korean Double Tax Agreements with OECD jurisdictions, the treaty-reduced rate is commonly 10% for interest and royalties, and 10% to 15% for dividends (typically 10% for a corporate shareholder holding 25% or more of the voting shares), subject to TRC, beneficial ownership, purpose tests, and the principal-purpose test; royalties are sourced to Korea based on the place of use or the place of registration of the intellectual property.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5 billion in cross-border related-party transactions triggers mandatory Local File preparation; Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required where the ultimate parent group's consolidated revenue equals or exceeds KRW 100 billion and the Korean entity's cross-border related-party transactions equal or exceed KRW 5 billion
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply the Caribbean/UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations as such, but enforces an equivalent substance-over-form doctrine and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Article 17 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. An M&A advisory boutique claiming treaty benefits, PE protection, or intercompany fee deductions must demonstrate that its Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) — deal origination, negotiation, financial modeling, execution of advisory mandates, board decision-making, and conflict resolution — are actually performed through genuine directors, employees, offices, bank accounts, and records in Korea; a shell entity without real economic substance is subject to re-characterization, denial of treaty relief, and piercing of the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting cross-border M&A success fees, recording fictitious expenses, diverting advisory revenue to offshore shell accounts, or materially understating the taxable base in the annual corporate income tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, Article 3 and Article 9: imprisonment of up to five years or a fine of up to twice the evaded tax; additionally, the National Tax Service imposes a 40% bad-faith underreporting surcharge, a 20% or 40% non-filing surcharge, and daily late-payment interest at the statutory rate; criminal referral is automatic for aggravated evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the company is operated as a sham: directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax under the secondary liability doctrine; personal assets are subject to civil restitution and confiscation; the directors are blacklisted as serious tax delinquents, which triggers a travel ban preventing departure from Korea until the deficiency is secured or paid; fraud-based evasion carries criminal imprisonment up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misdeclaration and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring client referral fees, management fees, or advisory success-fee sharing with foreign affiliated entities at non-arm's-length prices to shift Korean-source profit offshore, while failing to prepare, file, or contemporaneously substantiate the Local File, Master File, or Country-by-Country Report on post-inspection demand
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs penalties: failure to submit transfer pricing documentation attracts a monetary penalty of up to KRW 100 million; on re-determination, the tax authority imposes a surcharge of 10% of the adjusted underpaid corporate tax plus interest; the unfaithful-return surcharge may reach 40%; deliberate concealment of related-party transactions is referred for criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ordered the mispricing bear unlimited secondary liability for the resulting tax shortfall, with personal asset restraint orders and civil restitution demands; the director and the company are jointly designated as delinquent corporate taxpayers, generating a travel ban and blacklisting; if the scheme is proven fraudulent, the directors face criminal imprisonment up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and DTA Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, interest, or royalties to a foreign shareholder or affiliate without the statutory 22% withholding, or claiming a zero or reduced treaty rate through a nominee shareholder, conduit entity, or fabricated Tax Residency Certificate where the recipient is not the beneficial owner
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act withholding provisions make the Korean remitter personally liable for the un-withheld amount plus a 10% additional penalty; fraudulent claims are denied retroactively, requiring back-payment of the full 22% statutory rate with daily late-payment interest; Punishment of Tax Evaders Act criminal sanctions apply, including imprisonment up to five years and fines of up to twice the tax evaded; the National Tax Service may also impose civil penalties on the instrumentality used for treaty shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for the withholding deficiency, holding directors jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax; directors who signed or authorized the treaty-relief application face personal criminal liability, civil restitution of the diverted dividend or royalty amounts, asset confiscation, travel-ban blacklisting, and imprisonment up to five years where intent is shown.
